# HMAC/SHA-2 256/384/512 Design Specification

## 1. Scope

This specification describes the behavior of the HMAC/SHA-2 module. The module provides SHA-2 256/384/512 hashing and keyed HMAC authentication using those hash functions. It is intended to be used as a cryptographic hashing accelerator and is not hardened against side-channel or fault-injection attacks.

The specification covers only the local, externally observable behavior of the module: its register interface, message input behavior, hash operation flow, interrupts, error reporting, alert behavior, and idle indication.

## 2. Feature Summary

The module shall:

- Support unkeyed SHA-2 message digest computation with digest sizes of 256, 384, and 512 bits.
- Support keyed HMAC using SHA-2 256/384/512 as the underlying hash.
- Support secret key lengths of 128, 256, 384, 512, and 1024 bits, subject to the constraint that the key length shall not exceed the block size of the selected SHA-2 mode:
  - SHA-2 256 uses a 512-bit block, so 1024-bit HMAC keys are not supported.
  - SHA-2 384 and SHA-2 512 use a 1024-bit block, so all supported key lengths are allowed.
- Provide a software-accessible message FIFO with 32 word entries.
- Accept byte, half-word, and word writes to the message FIFO window.
- Compute SHA-2 padding internally. Software shall not be required to supply padding or message length to the hash operation.
- Provide interrupt outputs for hash completion, message FIFO empty status, and error notification.
- Provide a fatal alert output for TL-UL bus integrity faults.
- Provide an idle indicator output.

## 3. Interface Behavior

### 3.1 Reset

On reset, the module shall enter a known idle state:

- No hash operation shall be active.
- Hash-related interrupts shall be cleared.
- The message FIFO shall be empty.
- The SHA-2 engine and HMAC datapath shall be disabled by default.
- The default configured digest size and key length shall be treated as invalid until explicitly configured by software.
- The idle output shall indicate that the module is not yet advertising an idle state until the reset condition is released and the module has evaluated its internal state.

### 3.2 Register Interface

The module shall expose a TL-UL slave interface. Software accesses control, status, configuration, secret key, digest, message length, and wipe registers through this interface.

The message FIFO shall be accessed through a dedicated memory-mapped window. All addresses in that window shall map to the same FIFO entry point. The address bits needed to distinguish byte lanes shall be honored for sub-word writes.

Reads from the message FIFO window shall return a bus error.

When the message FIFO is full, writes shall not be dropped. The module shall apply back-pressure on the bus until space becomes available.

## 4. Configuration

### 4.1 Configuration Register

The module shall provide a configuration register with the following functional fields:

- HMAC enable: selects between keyed HMAC and unkeyed SHA-2.
- SHA-2 enable: enables or disables the SHA-2 engine.
- Digest size: selects SHA-2 256, SHA-2 384, or SHA-2 512.
- Key length: selects the HMAC secret key length.
- Endian swap: controls byte order conversion for message words written to the message FIFO.
- Digest swap: controls byte order conversion for digest words returned in digest registers.

The digest size and key length fields shall use one-hot encodings. Unsupported or invalid encodings shall be treated as invalid configuration. Starting a hash operation with an invalid digest size, or in HMAC mode with an invalid key length, shall be blocked and shall report an error.

### 4.2 Configuration Write Restrictions

Configuration register writes shall be accepted only when the module is in an idle state. Once a hash operation has been started or continued, the configuration shall be locked for the duration of that operation. Writes to the configuration register while locked shall be discarded.

The configuration lock shall be released when the module completes a hash operation or when a stop command reaches the intended stopping point.

### 4.3 SHA-2 Enable and Digest Register Access

When SHA-2 enable is deasserted:

- The SHA-2 engine shall not start or continue hashing.
- The digest registers shall be writable by software, allowing context restore.
- The digest contents shall be cleared when SHA-2 enable transitions from asserted to deasserted.

When SHA-2 enable is asserted:

- The digest registers shall be read-only from software’s perspective for normal hash operation.
- Starting or continuing hashing while SHA-2 enable is deasserted shall be treated as an error.

## 5. Secret Key Handling

### 5.1 Key Registers

The module shall provide 32 write-only secret key registers. Together they form a 1024-bit secret key. The registers shall be concatenated in ascending register order to form the key value.

The key registers shall be writable only while the module is idle. Writes to key registers while a hash operation is active shall be ignored and shall cause an error to be reported.

The key registers shall not be readable by software.

### 5.2 Key Length Validity

The configured key length shall be valid only if it is one of the supported values and is not larger than the block size of the selected digest mode.

For HMAC mode:

- SHA-2 256 shall allow 128-, 256-, 384-, and 512-bit keys.
- SHA-2 384 and SHA-2 512 shall allow 128-, 256-, 384-, 512-, and 1024-bit keys.

For unkeyed SHA-2 mode, the key length setting shall be ignored.

### 5.3 Long Secret Keys

If software requires an HMAC key larger than the supported maximum for the selected digest mode, software shall first reduce the key using a hash function and load the reduced value into the key registers. The module shall not accept an oversized key directly.

## 6. Hash and HMAC Operation

### 6.1 Starting an Operation

Software shall configure the module and, for HMAC mode, load the secret key before starting an operation.

A start command shall be accepted only when:

- SHA-2 enable is asserted.
- No hash operation is currently active.
- The configured digest size is valid.
- In HMAC mode, the configured key length is valid and supported for the selected digest size.

When a start command is accepted:

- The configuration and key registers shall be locked.
- The message length shall be reset to zero.
- The message FIFO shall be opened for software writes.
- The module shall begin the SHA-2 or HMAC computation from the initial state.

If a start command is attempted when these conditions are not met, no hash operation shall begin, and an error shall be reported.

### 6.2 Message Input

After a start or continue command has been accepted, software shall write the message data to the message FIFO.

The module shall:

- Coalesce sub-word writes into complete 32-bit words before hashing.
- Count the number of message bytes accepted and update the message length registers.
- Accept data until the process command is issued or until a stop command ends the active message phase.
- Continue accepting data while the FIFO has space, and apply bus back-pressure when the FIFO is full.

The message length shall be initialized to zero by a start command. A continue command shall not clear the message length; it shall resume from the restored context.

### 6.3 Endian Handling

The endian swap setting shall control the byte order within each 32-bit message word:

- When endian swap is deasserted, message words shall be consumed in the byte order supplied by software.
- When endian swap is asserted, the byte order of each 32-bit word shall be reversed before being used in the hash computation.

Byte-level writes shall not be affected by endian swap beyond their placement within the assembled word.

### 6.4 Process Command

A process command shall tell the module to finalize the current message and compute the final digest.

When a process command is accepted, the module shall:

- Stop accepting additional message data from software.
- Append the required SHA-2 padding and message length.
- Complete the hash computation.
- Update the digest registers.
- Raise the hash-done interrupt.

If HMAC mode is enabled, the module shall also perform the outer keyed hash computation required by HMAC before producing the final digest.

### 6.5 Stop Command

A stop command shall be used to pause operation at a message-block boundary for context switching.

When a stop command is accepted, the module shall:

- Stop accepting new message data after the current message block has been processed.
- Complete the current SHA-2 block computation.
- Leave the intermediate digest and message length available in the digest and message length registers.
- Release the configuration and key register lock so that software can change configuration or restore another context.
- Raise the hash-done interrupt when the stopping point is reached.

The stop command is not intended to finalize a message; it shall be used only for saving and restoring hashing context.

### 6.6 Continue Command

A continue command shall resume a previously saved hash context.

A continue command shall be accepted only when:

- SHA-2 enable is asserted.
- No hash operation is currently active.
- The digest registers and message length registers have been loaded with the saved context.
- The configured digest size is valid.

When a continue command is accepted:

- The configuration and key registers shall be locked.
- The message FIFO shall be opened for software writes.
- Hashing shall resume from the state represented by the digest registers and message length registers.
- The message length shall not be reset.

### 6.7 Digest Output

After a hash operation is complete, the digest shall be available in the digest registers.

The number of significant digest registers shall depend on the configured digest mode:

- SHA-2 256: 8 digest registers are significant.
- SHA-2 384: 12 digest registers are significant.
- SHA-2 512: 16 digest registers are significant.

The remaining digest registers in SHA-2 256 and SHA-2 384 modes shall not be considered meaningful and shall not be used by software.

The digest swap setting shall control byte order within each digest register. When digest swap is asserted, the bytes of each 32-bit digest word shall be reversed. The order of the digest registers shall remain unchanged.

### 6.8 Message Length Registers

The module shall maintain a 64-bit message length value that reflects the amount of message data received during the current hash operation.

The message length registers shall be:

- Automatically updated as message data is written to the message FIFO.
- Cleared by a start command.
- Retained across a stop command so software can save context.
- Writable by software when SHA-2 enable is deasserted, so software can restore context.

Software shall not need to write message length for normal hash operations.

## 7. Context Save and Restore

The module shall support interleaving multiple message streams through context switching.

To switch from one message stream to another, software shall:

1. Stop the current stream using the stop command.
2. Wait for the hash-done interrupt.
3. Save the digest registers, message length registers, configuration, and any secret key values kept by software.
4. Disable SHA-2 enable, which clears the digest registers.
5. Configure and start or continue another stream.
6. Before resuming the saved stream, disable SHA-2 enable.
7. Restore the saved configuration, digest registers, and message length registers.
8. Re-enable SHA-2 enable.
9. Issue the continue command.

The module shall make this possible by:

- Retaining digest and message length values across a stop command.
- Allowing digest and message length registers to be written when SHA-2 enable is deasserted.
- Allowing the configuration to be updated when the module is idle or after a stop.
- Not clearing the message length on continue.

## 8. Message FIFO Status

The module shall provide status information about the message FIFO:

- FIFO empty: asserted when the message FIFO contains no data.
- FIFO full: asserted when the message FIFO has no free entries.
- FIFO depth: reports the number of entries currently occupied in the message FIFO.

After reset, the message FIFO shall be empty.

## 9. Interrupts

The module shall provide three interrupt outputs:

### 9.1 Hash Done Interrupt

The hash-done interrupt shall be raised when a hash operation reaches a point at which a valid digest is available:

- After a process command completes.
- After a stop command reaches the intended stopping point.

The hash-done interrupt shall be a sticky event interrupt. Its state shall be cleared by software writing 1 to the corresponding interrupt state bit.

### 9.2 FIFO Empty Interrupt

The FIFO-empty interrupt is a status interrupt, not a completion event.

It shall be raised when:

- The message FIFO becomes empty.
- The message FIFO is in a state where software can usefully write more data.
- The message FIFO had previously become full during the current message-write phase.

It shall be suppressed when:

- Software message input is not currently allowed.
- A process or stop command has ended the active software message-write phase.
- The hardware is internally managing the message FIFO for HMAC computation.
- The message FIFO had not previously been full since the last start, continue, process, or stop command.

### 9.3 Error Interrupt

The error interrupt shall be raised when the module detects an illegal software access or an invalid operation.

The error interrupt shall be a sticky event interrupt. Its state shall be cleared by software writing 1 to the corresponding interrupt state bit.

The error interrupt shall be generated regardless of whether the interrupt output is enabled. The interrupt enable bit only gates the output, not the recorded state.

### 9.4 Interrupt Enable and Test

The module shall provide interrupt enable registers and interrupt test registers for each interrupt.

Writing 1 to an interrupt test bit shall cause the corresponding interrupt state to be set, allowing software to verify interrupt connectivity.

Writing 1 to an interrupt enable bit shall allow the corresponding interrupt to propagate to the interrupt output.

## 10. Error Reporting

When an error condition is detected, the module shall:

- Set the error interrupt state.
- Record an error code in the error code register.

The following conditions shall be reported as errors:

- A start or continue command is issued while SHA-2 enable is deasserted.
- A start or continue command is issued while a hash operation is already active.
- A start command is issued with an invalid configuration, including:
  - Invalid or unsupported digest size.
  - HMAC mode with invalid or unsupported key length.
  - HMAC mode with a 1024-bit key while SHA-2 256 is selected.
- Software writes to any secret key register while a hash operation is active.
- Software accesses the message FIFO when message input is not allowed.

The module shall record only the first error condition while the error interrupt state is pending. If software has not cleared the error interrupt state, subsequent error events shall not overwrite the recorded error code.

The error code register shall be read-only.

## 11. Alert Behavior

The module shall provide a fatal fault alert.

The fatal fault alert shall be raised when the TL-UL register interface detects a bus integrity violation.

The module shall also provide an alert test register. Writing 1 to the alert test bit shall cause the alert output to be exercised in the same manner as a real alert event.

## 12. Idle Indication

The module shall provide an idle output using a multi-bit boolean encoding.

The idle output shall be asserted only when:

- No hash operation is active.
- No message data remains queued in the message FIFO.
- No partial message word is still being accumulated in the input path.
- The HMAC and SHA-2 datapaths are idle.

The idle output shall be deasserted during reset and shall remain deasserted until the module is in its idle state.

The idle indication is intended for use by system-level power management or other modules that need to know when the HMAC module has completed all internal work.

## 13. Cryptographic Behavior

### 13.1 SHA-2 Mode

When configured for unkeyed SHA-2 mode, the module shall compute the SHA-2 digest of the message written to the message FIFO after the most recent start or continue command.

The result shall match the SHA-2 256, SHA-2 384, or SHA-2 512 algorithm as defined by FIPS 180-4.

The secret key shall not affect the digest in this mode.

### 13.2 HMAC Mode

When configured for HMAC mode, the module shall compute the HMAC of the message using the configured secret key and the selected SHA-2 digest size.

The result shall match the HMAC algorithm as defined by FIPS 198-1.

The module shall internally perform the required two hash computations:

- The first computation shall use the inner-padded key followed by the message.
- The second computation shall use the outer-padded key followed by the first digest.

The module shall handle key padding internally. If the configured key length is shorter than the block size, the key shall be zero-padded to the block size before applying the HMAC inner and outer pads.

If the configured key length exceeds the block size, the start command shall be blocked and an error shall be reported.

# HMAC Core Module Specification

## 1. Purpose

The HMAC core module implements the control and data-path behavior for a SHA-2 based hash engine that can operate in two modes:

- **Unkeyed SHA-2 mode**: the module passes message data through to the hash engine without adding key material.
- **Keyed HMAC mode**: the module performs the two-round HMAC construction using a secret key, inner and outer padding, the incoming message, and the first-round digest.

The module supports SHA-2 256, SHA-2 384, and SHA-2 512 digest modes. In SHA-2 256 mode, the block size is 512 bits. In SHA-2 384 and SHA-2 512 modes, the block size is 1024 bits.

## 2. Reset and Initial State

After reset, the module must be idle and must not assert hash completion. It must not present any internally generated message data to the hash engine. The module must be ready to accept a new start command once it is idle.

## 3. Unkeyed SHA-2 Mode

When HMAC is disabled, the module must behave as a transparent data path between the incoming message FIFO and the hash engine.

In this mode:

- Incoming message words must be passed through unchanged.
- Start, continue, and process requests must be forwarded to the hash engine.
- The completion indication from the hash engine must be reported as the final hash-completion indication.
- The message length presented to the hash engine must be the externally supplied message length without any adjustment.

The module must not modify, reorder, or drop message data in unkeyed mode.

## 4. Keyed HMAC Mode

When HMAC is enabled, the module must perform the complete HMAC computation in the following order:

1. Present the inner-padded key block to the hash engine.
2. Present the user message from the incoming message FIFO.
3. Wait for the first-round hash to complete.
4. Copy the first-round digest into the internal message FIFO path.
5. Present the outer-padded key block to the hash engine.
6. Present the stored first-round digest as message data.
7. Wait for the second-round hash to complete.
8. Assert the final HMAC completion indication.

The final completion indication must only be asserted after the second round completes. The module must not report the first-round completion as the final HMAC completion.

### 4.1 Inner and Outer Padding

The module must construct the inner-padded key and outer-padded key from the configured secret key.

For both pads:

- The selected key bits must be placed at the most-significant end of the block.
- The remaining low-order bits of the block must be zero-filled.
- The entire block must be XORed with a repeated byte pattern.
- The inner pad must use the byte pattern `0x36`.
- The outer pad must use the byte pattern `0x5c`.

The block width must match the configured digest mode:

- SHA-2 256: 512-bit block.
- SHA-2 384: 1024-bit block.
- SHA-2 512: 1024-bit block.

The valid key lengths are:

| Digest mode  | Supported key lengths                 |
|--------------|---------------------------------------|
| SHA-2 256    | 128, 256, 384, 512 bits               |
| SHA-2 384    | 128, 256, 384, 512, 1024 bits         |
| SHA-2 512    | 128, 256, 384, 512, 1024 bits         |

A 1024-bit key is not usable with SHA-2 256 because it exceeds the 512-bit block size.

## 5. HMAC Round and Phase Behavior

### 5.1 First Round

When a start command is accepted in HMAC mode, the module must begin by feeding exactly one block of inner-padded key data to the hash engine. After that block has been delivered, it must switch to forwarding message data from the incoming message FIFO.

The module must track how much data has been delivered for the active hash operation. It must stop delivering message data once the total amount of data expected for the first round has been delivered. The total expected first-round data length is:

- SHA-2 256: software message length + 512 bits.
- SHA-2 384: software message length + 1024 bits.
- SHA-2 512: software message length + 1024 bits.

The extra block size accounts for the inner-padded key block, which is not included in the software-visible message length.

### 5.2 Process Request in First Round

When a process request is received in the first round, the module must allow any remaining valid message words to be delivered up to the expected first-round length. It must then stop delivering data and wait for the hash engine to complete the first-round digest.

If the message is empty, or if all message data has already been delivered, the module must proceed directly to waiting for first-round completion when the process request is received.

### 5.3 Digest Transfer

After the first-round hash completes, the module must write the first-round digest into the internal message FIFO path. The number of digest words written must match the selected digest size:

- SHA-2 256: 8 words.
- SHA-2 384: 12 words.
- SHA-2 512: 16 words.

The words must be written in the correct digest word order. The module must not advance to the next word until the current word is accepted.

### 5.4 Second Round

After the first-round digest has been stored, the module must start a new hash operation for the second round.

The module must feed exactly one block of outer-padded key data to the hash engine. After that block has been delivered, it must feed the stored first-round digest words as the message data.

The total expected second-round data length is fixed:

| Digest mode  | Second-round message length |
|--------------|-----------------------------|
| SHA-2 256    | 512 + 256 = 768 bits        |
| SHA-2 384    | 1024 + 384 = 1408 bits      |
| SHA-2 512    | 1024 + 512 = 1536 bits      |

When all second-round data has been delivered, the module must automatically request the hash engine to finish the hash operation. After the second-round hash completes, the module must assert the final HMAC completion indication.

## 6. Message Length Reporting

The message length value presented to the hash engine must be correct for the active round.

- In unkeyed SHA-2 mode, the presented message length must be the externally supplied message length.
- In HMAC first round, the presented message length must be the externally supplied message length plus one block size.
- In HMAC second round, the presented message length must be the fixed value equal to one block size plus the selected digest size.

The module must not use the software message length directly as the SHA-2 message length during HMAC rounds, because the length must include the padding and digest data inserted by the HMAC construction.

## 7. Continue and Context-Switch Behavior

The module must support saving and restoring the hashing context at a message-block boundary.

When a continue request is accepted in HMAC mode, the module must not restart the HMAC sequence from the beginning. Instead, it must continue from the message phase of the first round, using the restored hash context and the restored software message length.

While continuing, the first-round expected length must again be the restored software message length plus one block size.

A continue request is accepted in the first-round message phase. The module is not required to accept or act on a continue request during the second round.

## 8. Stop and Idle Indication

The module must indicate when it is idle.

The idle indication must be deasserted when a start or continue request is accepted. The module must return to the idle state after the final HMAC or SHA-2 operation completes.

When a stop request is received at a message-block boundary during the message phase, the module must assert the idle indication so that software can save the current hashing context. After a later continue request, the module must resume operation from that context.

## 9. Data Integrity and Flow Control

The module must preserve data integrity under all flow-control conditions.

- A data word must not be presented more than once.
- A data word must not be skipped.
- When a destination is not ready to accept a word, the module must hold the current word and must not advance to the next word.
- When the incoming message FIFO has no data available, the module must not indicate that message data is available to the hash engine.
- During the pad-feeding phases, the module must generate exactly one block of pad data and must stop at the block boundary.
- During the message phases, the module must stop presenting data once the expected length for the active round has been reached.

## 10. Summary of Behavior

In normal operation, the module must produce the following behavior:

| Phase                       | Data source                      | Hash engine message length               |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| HMAC first round, pad block | Inner-padded key                 | Software message length + block size     |
| HMAC first round, message   | Incoming message FIFO            | Software message length + block size     |
| HMAC digest transfer        | First-round digest               | Not applicable                           |
| HMAC second round, pad block| Outer-padded key                 | Block size + digest size                 |
| HMAC second round, message  | Stored first-round digest        | Block size + digest size                 |
| Unkeyed SHA-2 mode          | Incoming message FIFO            | Software message length                  |

This behavior ensures that the module correctly implements both unkeyed SHA-2 acceleration and the full HMAC construction for all supported digest and key configurations.
